governing: steel.bolts: bolt shear of the most loaded beam-side bolt, elastic method with e = a = 4.125 in (AISC 360-22 J3.7)
notes: Design: WT7x11 A992 shear tee, 7.5 in long, bolted to the W10x49 column flange and to the W12x26 beam web, ASD. Bolts are 3/4 in A325-N (Group 120, threads included, snug tight) in standard holes: 2 rows at 4 in pitch through the stem and beam web, and 4 through the tee flange at a 2-7/8 in gauge. Edge distance at the tee ends is 1-3/4 in. The bolt line is a = 4-1/8 in from the back of the tee flange, the beam-web edge distance is 2-1/2 in (so the beam end sits 1-5/8 in from the column face), and the top bolt is 3 in below the top of the beam. Petra check: PASS, 16 of 16 obligations certified, for shear 0 to 9.817 kip service. Governing strength check: beam-side bolt, demand 11.25 kip against 11.93 kip bolt shear (0.943). Other strength checks: flexural rupture of the stem 0.513, block shear 0.489, stem shear rupture 0.381. Three detailing limits are close and must be built as drawn. (1) Stem-toe edge distance is 2.725 in against the J3.6 maximum of 12t = 2.76 in (0.987), so do not reduce a or substitute a deeper tee. (2) Tee-flange edge distance is 1-1/16 in against the 1 in minimum (0.941). (3) Bolt clearance to the column web is at 0.964, so hold the 2-7/8 in gauge. Petra excused its tee_ductility check. By hand, Manual Part 9 dmin = min(0.163 tf sqrt(Fy/b (b^2/L^2 + 2)), 0.69 sqrt(ts)) is about min(0.66, 0.33) = 0.33 in, which is below 0.75 in, and the stem (0.23 in) is thinner than d/2 + 1/16 = 0.4375 in. Shear yielding of the uncoped W12x26 web is not in Petra's table; by hand it is about 9.8/56 = 0.18. A heavier alternative (WT6x13, 7 in long, 3.5 in pitch) also passed, at 0.894.
